function: Learned joint design of AP precoding, RIS phase shifts and harvest/reflect time scheduling to maximize power harvested by RISs under per-user SINR constraints (p. 3).
system: Cell-free mMIMO: L APs with Nt antennas, K users, N distributed RISs of M elements; reflecting RIS with RF-to-DC harvesting, time-switched EH or reflection; band not stated (p. 2).
method: Clipped TD3 deep reinforcement learning (actor-critic, twin critics, replay buffer, decaying noise clipping), trained by interaction with the simulated environment; reinforcement paradigm (p. 4).
data_channel: Own simulator: AP-user links Rayleigh with path-loss exponent 4, RIS-cascaded links Rician with exponent 2.5, nodes in 0.2 x 0.2 km area; no dataset or measurements (p. 5).
test_conditions: Same simulated setting for training and evaluation (Table I: 5,000,000 steps); sweeps over RIS elements, AP power, number of APs, EMI power; no unseen scenario (p. 5).
baselines: Learned: clipped DDPG; TD3 without clipped actions (variant of proposed). Non-learned alternating optimization appears only in the complexity analysis, not in performance plots (p. 5).
metrics: Instant reward (training curve), harvested power of RISs in dBm, normalized harvested power E_h/L, versus RIS elements, AP transmit power, number of APs and EMI power (p. 5).
complexity: Big-O of AO (O(K^5.5 L^4.5 Nt^4) for W), DDPG and proposed TD3 in network layer sizes; DRL stated much lower; no runtime or parameter count (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 5: "direct channels follow Rayleigh distribution with a path-loss" (RIS links Rician): custom simulator; no 3GPP TR 38.901, DeepMIMO or COST 2100 model and no measured data is named anywhere.
q2_support: p. 5: "Fig. 3 shows the harvested power of RISs versus the number of RIS" elements and EMI power; Fig. 4 sweeps AP power and APs. Only sweeps in one simulator; no trained agent is tested on an unseen scenario or adapted.
q3_support: p. 5: "By comparing the complexity of the above schemes, it is obvious" - the non-learned AO (p. 4) is compared on complexity only; Figs. 2 and 4 compare harvested power only with TD3 and clipped DDPG, so no non-learned baseline on performance.
q4_support: p. 4: "Thus, its computational complexity is given by" a big-O expression for the proposed clipped TD3, after the orders of AO and DDPG.
q5_support: p. 5: "direct channels follow Rayleigh distribution with a path-loss" - own simulated channels; no code or data link, DOI or availability statement in pp. 1-6, and no public or measured dataset.
notes: Correspondence (IEEE TVT 75(2), Feb 2026); title and DOI on p. 1 match. Area 3: TD3 outputs AP precoder, RIS phase shifts and harvest/reflect time split; objective is harvested power under SINR constraints. RIS is reflecting with per-element RF-to-DC harvesting and STAR-inspired time switching (p. 3), not a STAR-RIS. 'TD3 w/o clipped action' (Fig. 2) is a variant of the proposed method, so it is not the learned baseline of q3; clipped DDPG is (standard algorithm on the same problem), but the only non-learned method, AO (p. 4), is compared on complexity alone, hence q3 = 0. Perfect CSI assumed (p. 2). Table I and Figs. 2-4 read from the page image.
